tools.name: open_page
tools.description: Use this tool to fetch text content from any website URL. Returns the complete page if no line range is specified up to truncation.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: The URL of the webpage to open.

parameters.name: start_line
parameters.description: Optional starting line number (1-indexed). If provided, returns content from this line to the end of the page.

tools.name: open_page_with_find
tools.description: Fetch text content from a website URL. If a regex pattern is provided, returns matching lines with line numbers and surrounding context. If no pattern is provided, returns the full page content.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: The URL of the webpage to open.

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: Optional regular expression pattern to search for in the page content. Use standard regex syntax. Search is case-insensitive. If not provided, returns the full page content.

parameters.name: max_matches
parameters.description: Maximum number of matches to return. Defaults to 50.

parameters.name: context_lines
parameters.description: Number of context lines to show before and after each match. Defaults to 10.

tools.name: view_image
tools.description: Look at an image at a given url. Returns the image and an image id.

parameters.name: image_url
parameters.description: The URL of the image to view.

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: This action allows you to search the web. You can use search operators like site:reddit.com when needed.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: The search query to look up on the web.

parameters.name: num_results
parameters.description: The number of results to return. It is optional, default 10, max is 30.

tools.name: x_keyword_search
tools.description: Advanced search tool for X Posts.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description:
The search query string for X advanced search. Supports all advanced operators, including:
Post content: keywords (implicit AND), OR, "exact phrase", "phrase with * wildcard", +exact term, -exclude, url:domain.
From/to/mentions: from:user, to:user, @user, list:id or list:slug.
Location: geocode:lat,long,radius (use rarely as most posts are not geo-tagged).
Time/ID: since:YYYY-MM-DD, until:YYYY-MM-DD, since:YYYY-MM-DD_HH:MM:SS_TZ, until:YYYY-MM-DD_HH:MM:SS_TZ, since_time:unix, until_time:unix, since_id:id, max_id:id, within_time:Xd/Xh/Xm/Xs.
Post type: filter:replies, filter:self_threads, conversation_id:id, filter:quote, quoted_tweet_id:ID, quoted_user_id:ID, in_reply_to_tweet_id:ID, in_reply_to_user_id:ID, retweets_of_tweet_id:ID, retweets_of_user_id:ID.
Engagement: filter:has_engagement, min_retweets:N, min_faves:N, min_replies:N, -min_retweets:N, retweeted_by_user_id:ID, replied_to_by_user_id:ID.
Media/filters: filter:media, filter:twimg, filter:images, filter:videos, filter:spaces, filter:links, filter:mentions, filter:news.
Most filters can be negated with -. Use parentheses for grouping. Spaces mean AND; OR must be uppercase.

Example query:
(puppy OR kitten) (sweet OR cute) filter:images min_faves:10

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The number of posts to return. Default to 3, max is 10.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Sort by Top or Latest. The default is Top. You must output the mode with a capital first letter.

tools.description: Fetch X posts that are relevant to a semantic search query.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: A semantic search query to find relevant related posts

parameters.name: limit

parameters.name: from_date

parameters.name: to_date

parameters.name: exclude_usernames

parameters.name: usernames
parameters.description: Optional: Filter to only include these usernames.

parameters.name: min_score_threshold
parameters.description: Optional: Minimum relevancy score threshold for posts.

tools.name: x_user_search
tools.description: Search for an X user given a search query.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: The name or account you are searching for

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Number of users to return. default to 3.

tools.name: x_thread_fetch
tools.description: Fetch the content of an X post and the context around it, including parent posts and replies.

parameters.name: post_id
parameters.description: The ID of the post to fetch along with its context.

tools.name: view_x_video
tools.description: View the interleaved frames and subtitles of a video on X. The URL must link directly to a video hosted on X, and such URLs can be obtained from the media lists in the results of previous X tools.

parameters.name: video_url
parameters.description: The url of the video you wish to view.

tools.name: search_connected_tools
tools.description: Search the user's connected services for available tools. The user has these services connected: Voice (generate spoken audio from text), Automations (schedule a prompt for Grok to run later, once or on a repeating cadence). Only use this for the user's connected services — not for your built-in tools which you can call directly. Call this when the user needs to interact with any of these services. Describe the ACTION you need (e.g., 'search pages', 'send message', 'create issue', 'list files'). Returns ranked results with full argument schemas so you can call_connected_tool immediately. If the user needs a service that is not connected, call list_available_connectors. If it returns names, pass one of them to request_connector_auth; do not invent names. If the list is empty, use the name the user said or the name from an auth error.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Describe the action to perform using keywords that match tool names and descriptions. Good examples: 'search pages', 'create issue', 'send message', 'list files', 'read email', 'calendar events', 'query database'. Bad examples: 'what tools are available', 'my connected apps', 'list integrations'.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of tools to return (default: 10, max: 20). Use a higher limit when exploring available capabilities.

tools.name: call_connected_tool
tools.description: Execute a connected tool by name with JSON arguments. Only for tools discovered via search_connected_tools — not for your built-in tools. Always use search_connected_tools first to find the right tool and get its argument schema. Pass the tool name exactly as returned by search_connected_tools.

parameters.name: tool_name
parameters.description: The exact tool name as returned by search_connected_tools results.

parameters.name: arguments
parameters.description: JSON object containing the arguments to pass to the tool. Check the input_schema from search results.

tools.name: list_available_connectors
tools.description: List services the user can connect but has not connected yet. Call this when search_connected_tools finds nothing for a service the user asked about, before request_connector_auth. Returns display names to pass to request_connector_auth. Do not invent names that are not in the result.

parameters.description: The file path to read

parameters.name: offset

parameters.description: The path to the file to modify

parameters.name: old_string

parameters.name: new_string

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Executes a given bash command in a fresh shell at the session working directory.

parameters.name: command
parameters.description: The command to execute

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: One sentence explanation as to why this command needs to be run and how it contributes to the goal.

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description: Timeout in seconds

tools.name: browser_tab
tools.description: Loads a URL or interacts with an existing tab. Optionally runs JS and captures network, console logs, and screenshots.

parameters.name: tabId
parameters.description: Existing tab ID. If omitted, creates a new one

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: URL to navigate to if needed

parameters.name: refresh
parameters.description: Refresh the tab before executing the code

parameters.name: waitTime
parameters.description: Wait time after load before executing the code in seconds

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description: Timeout for JS execution in seconds

parameters.name: includeNetwork
parameters.description: Include network summaries

parameters.name: includeLogs
parameters.description: Include console logs

parameters.name: screenshot
parameters.description: Include a screenshot of the page with device emulation: 'mobile', 'desktop', or 'both'

tools.name: browser_network_details
tools.description: Returns headers and body for a network request captured by browser_tab (requires includeNetwork=true). Writes files and returns paths.

parameters.name: tabId
parameters.description: Existing tab ID

parameters.name: requestId
parameters.description: Specific request ID for details (defaults to latest if omitted)

tools.name: request_connector_auth
tools.description:
Show the user an in-chat card to connect or reauthenticate a connector. Call this only when the current user request cannot be completed without that connector, and either: (1) the user has never connected it, or (2) a connected-tool or search_connected_tools result says auth expired or needs re-authentication.
Do not call speculatively, "just in case", or for a connector that already worked this turn. Do not call more than once per connector per turn. If several connectors could work, pick the single one this ask needs.
If search finds nothing, call list_available_connectors and pass one of its names. If that list is empty, use the user's or auth-error name.
After {"status":"connected"}, call search_connected_tools for the original task and then call_connected_tool. If search finds nothing, tell the user the connector is not ready yet — do not invent a workaround unless they ask.
On skipped / timeout / unavailable, continue without the connector. Do not work around it unless they ask.
Success is {"status":"connected"|"skipped","connector":"<id>"}. On denial or failure: {"error":"permission_denied"|"unavailable"|"user_cancelled"|"unknown_connector"}. The server waits up to timeout_secs then synthesizes {"error":"client_tool_timeout"}.

parameters.name: connector
parameters.description: Display name from list_available_connectors, the user, or an auth-error (e.g. "Linear"). Not a UUID.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.description: Short reason shown on the connect card, in the user's terms, explaining why this connector is needed.
